objective: Bridge a support case to the artifacts the runtime produces: creating an S0 or S1 case opens an incident hold against its run identifier and unit serial in the same operation, closing a case does not release the hold, and release is a separate recorded action.
decision_supported: Can an incident's evidence be destroyed by ordinary retention while the case that needs it is still open, and is the answer produced by the existing governance rule rather than a second one written for support?
acceptance: A support case is created with a severity, and creating an S0 or S1 case opens a hold against the run identifier and the unit serial in the same operation, so a case cannot exist unbacked.
A hold that cannot be opened leaves no case and no partial hold behind: the rollback releases only what that call opened, not a pre-existing hold with the same identifier.
The hold blocks deletion of the case's evidence classes even after their retention expires, and deletion_decision reports the hold as the reason.
S3 cases open no hold and say so through holds_evidence being false, so a cosmetic defect cannot hold evidence forever.
Closing a case does not silently release the hold: release is a separate, recorded action with an author, a reason and a timestamp, matching HoldRegister.release semantics.
The case record references evidence by the identifiers the runtime already uses (run_id, configuration_hash), not by copied file paths.
A case whose run identifier does not exist is refused at creation rather than accepted and discovered missing during the investigation.
case-template.csv gains the columns this needs; escalation-matrix.csv is unchanged.
The retention table and GOVERNANCE_RULES_VERSION are unchanged, and test_data_governance.py passes untouched.
evidence: pytest output for tests/unit/test_support_case.py: 27 passed, covering the S0 hold, the S3 no-hold case, the separated release, the unknown-run refusal and the rollback of a partially opened hold.
pytest output for tests/unit/test_data_governance.py: 34 passed unchanged, which is the evidence that the policy table did not move.
A recorded S0 case with its two holds and the deletion_decision output showing the hold as the reason deletion is refused after 400 days.
make docs PASS, ruff check and ruff format --check clean.
A full make test comparison against the unmodified main baseline showing the same pre-existing environment-blocked failures and no new ones.
stop_conditions: The work would require changing a retention value or GOVERNANCE_RULES_VERSION; that table is versioned and changing it is its own issue with the data owner.
The work would require a change to libs/application/workbench/application/data_governance.py behaviour rather than consuming it.
A write outside allowed_paths is required, especially to escalation-matrix.csv or to any governance module.

Answering the severity question would require a product decision about which severities hold evidence; the issue's own table and escalation matrix already answer it, so a disagreement there is a stop rather than a silent choice.
data_classification: Repository-local Python and CSV. The module handles run and unit identifiers and a symptom narrative; it reads no credentials, writes no personal data and copies no evidence paths.
model_policy: Deterministic Python and a local pytest run; no model inference and no network access added by this change.
risks_and_fallbacks: Holding the wrong evidence class would either over-retain or leave an incident unprotected. The module holds run_event_log, hardware_record and release_evidence, and deliberately not camera_evidence, which is the class the 30-day retention is written for; holding every frame of every S0 case would cover more than the investigation needs.

Two holds per case could be mistaken for a wildcard. They are scoped to the run and the unit separately so a case about one unit does not protect every other run, and a test asserts that a second run is not covered.
A caller could pass no run index and skip the unknown-run check. That is recorded rather than hidden: known_runs=None means the caller has no index, and the check is the caller's to supply.

Rollback is a revert of this commit: stop opening holds at case creation. Existing holds stay visible and releasable, so nothing becomes permanently undeletable, and the governance table is untouched.
